subject: Problem with density fit, mask and its covariates

messages.author: 6fd86ca703710ed8
messages.subject: Problem with density fit, mask and its covariates
parts:
Hi,
I am trying to model density of jaguars by different years (3) and I first run the detection and sigma to get the best models. Then I created 3 different masks for each session (years).
Problem is when I tried the different models for density, it just end up giving me the same exact values for all models and not getting into consideration the Density part of it. I have the feeling that it may be due to the way I am adding the mask but I am not sure as it is the first time I'm doing it.
Here is the code from the mask part on:

mask_1<-read.mask("Mask_1s.csv", spacing = 500, header=TRUE,columns=c("NDVI","dWater"))
mask_2<-read.mask("Mask_2s.csv", spacing = 500, header=TRUE,columns=c("NDVI","dWater"))
mask_3<-read.mask("Mask_3s.csv", spacing = 500, header=TRUE,columns=c("NDVI","dWater"))

mask=list("Sess1" =mask_1,"Sess2" =mask_2,"Sess3" =mask_3)

All_Jag=MS.capthist(Sess1,Sess2,Sess3)
summary(All_Jag, terse = TRUE)

fits6a <- secr.fit(All_Jag,model=list(D~1,g0~Prey,sigma~session),mask=mask, trace = FALSE,verify=FALSE,CL=TRUE,details = list(fastproximity = FALSE))
fits6b <- secr.fit(All_Jag,model=list(D~NDVI,g0~Prey,sigma~session),mask=mask, trace = FALSE,verify=FALSE,CL=TRUE,details = list(fastproximity = FALSE))
fits6c <- secr.fit(All_Jag,model=list(D~dWater,g0~Prey,sigma~session),mask=mask, trace = FALSE,verify=FALSE,CL=TRUE,details = list(fastproximity = FALSE))
fits6d <- secr.fit(All_Jag,model=list(D~NDVI+dWater,g0~Prey,sigma~session),mask=mask, trace = FALSE,verify=FALSE,CL=TRUE,details = list(fastproximity = FALSE))
                   
AicsJagD1=AIC(fits6a,fits6b,fits6c,fits6d)
AicsJagD1

First of this I was trying a different way for the masks but was getting a warning and still the same values for all models. Now I don't get warnings but still the same result.

mask_1<-read.csv("Mask_1s.csv")
mask1<-read.mask(data=mask_1, spacing = 500, header=TRUE)

mask_2<-read.csv("Mask_2s.csv")
mask2<-read.mask(data=mask_2, spacing = 500, header=TRUE)
mask_3<-read.csv("Mask_3s.csv")
mask3<-read.mask(data=mask_3, spacing = 500, header=TRUE)

msk1=read.mask(data=mask1,spacing = 500, header = TRUE,columns=c("NDVI","dWater"))
msk2=read.mask(data=mask2,spacing = 500, header = TRUE,columns=c("NDVI","dWater"))
msk3=read.mask(data=mask3,spacing = 500, header = TRUE,columns=c("NDVI","dWater"))

mask=list(msk1,msk2,msk3)

All_Jag=MS.capthist(Sess1,Sess2,Sess3)
summary(All_Jag, terse = TRUE)

fits6a <- secr.fit(All_Jag,model=list(D~1,g0~Prey,sigma~session),mask=mask, trace = FALSE,verify=FALSE,CL=TRUE,details = list(fastproximity = FALSE,contrasts = list(session = MASS::contr.sdif)))

#WARNING
#1: In model.matrix.default(formula, data = data, contrasts.arg = contrasts) :
  #variable 'session' is absent, its contrast will be ignored

Can someone please give me some light in what I am doing wrong?
Thanks!

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Problem with density fit, mask and its covariates
parts:
Hello Bardales

I assume you surveyed substantially different areas in the three years, or the covariates changed between years. If you surveyed essentially the same area and covariates did not change then I would use the same mask to save some of the messing about.

You cannot model density (D ~ NDVI etc.) in a conditional model (CL = TRUE) (incidentally, it would be easier to read the code if you used spaces).
I suggest dropping the whole 'details' argument at least for a start - I don't see why you cannot use the fastproximity method, and contrasts.arg is giving trouble. (The handling of contrasts did change recently so there may be a real issue there, but let's strip out unnecessary stuff).

Regards
Murray
